results.title: Accra after Sunset: El Niño, a heating city and the sky above us
results.content: The sun has gone down, but the room still feels hot. The fan is running, yet sleep does not come easily. Outside, people seek relief on verandas, in compound yards and along the roadside. For anyone who has spent such an evening in Accra, the question is simple: why does sunset bring so little comfort? That question has become more urgent. On 30 October 2026, the Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet) warned that a very strong and still intensifying El Niño is developing, and that Ghana should prepare for a hotter, drier and dustier dry season. Heat stress is expected to peak between February and April 2027, especially in the north. The ocean data behind that warning are striking. In mid-October, the weekly Niño 3.4 index, the standard measure of El Niño, reached +3.3°C. Scientists classify anything above +2.0°C as "very strong."

results.title: Appoint Clowns. Get a Circus
results.content: One of the biggest obstacles to Ghana’s economic and social development is not a shortage of ideas, policies or even resources. It is the chronic appointment of incompetent people to positions that demand competence, leadership and results. Take our Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives. For decades, many have presided over communities that remain filthy, poorly planned, environmentally deplorable and barely liveable. Roads are neglected, drains remain choked, sanitation is appalling, public spaces are abandoned and basic urban management appears to be an alien concept.

results.title: 17-year-old charged with murder over killing of Ghanaian teenager Javits Frimpong in New York
results.content: A 17-year-old has been charged with murder in connection with the fatal shooting of 15-year-old Ghanaian boy Javits Frimpong in the Bronx, New York. The New York Police Department (NYPD) said detectives arrested the suspect on Wednesday morning and took him to the 42nd Precinct for questioning before charging him with murder. Javits was shot in the stomach near Crotona Park on October 29, 2026. Police officers rushed him to St. Barnabas Hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The suspect's identity has not been released because he is a minor. The NYPD says it is still searching for other people who may have been connected to the shooting. Javits' father, Thomas Frimpong, said he was relieved that a suspect had been charged. Speaking emotionally at a press conference on Wednesday, he recalled that he was at work when he received news that his son had been shot.
